answer_1.quote: Evaluating the quality of outputs produced by language models (LMs) is progressively becoming difficult, as the outputs cover an extremely diverse distribution of text and complex tasks.
answer_1.outputs: Text responses generated by LMs for chat instructions

answer_2.quote: We use Pearson, Spearman, and Kendall-Tau as performance metrics to measure scoring correlations against reference evaluators.

answer_3.quote: In this paradigm, LMs are either prompted to output a scalar indicator of quality (denoted as direct assessment) or to determine which of two outputs are preferred (denoted as pairwise ranking).

answer_4.quote: we employ five annotators with backgrounds in natural language processing. The annotation study was designed and administered in accordance with [Affiliation X]'s ethical guidelines.
answer_4.guideline: Assess coherence of verbal feedback with scoring decisions, suitability against evaluation criteria, and criticality compared to concatenated feedback.
